questions.skill: Prove that all circles are similar
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Circle C has center A and radius r, and circle D has center B and radius s. Prove that the two circles are similar.
questions.prompt_markup: Circle C has center A and radius r, and circle D has center B and radius s. Prove that the two circles are similar.
questions.correct_answer: A translation followed by a dilation maps C onto D, so they are similar.
questions.required_method: Translate A to B, then dilate about B with scale factor s/r. Show the image of C is exactly D.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: (1) the translation maps C onto the circle with center B and radius r (distances kept); (2) the dilation about B with factor s/r maps each point at distance r from B to a point at distance s on the same ray, so onto D; (3) every point of D is reached (the inverse dilation); a similarity transformation exists. Invalid: "circles all look alike"; only checking two specific circles.

questions.prompt: Circle C₁ has center (0, 0) and radius 2. Circle C₂ has center (3, -1) and radius 5. Prove that C₁ and C₂ are similar by giving a similarity transformation, and show where it sends the point (2, 0) of C₁.

questions.correct_answer: Translate by (x, y) → (x + 3, y - 1), then dilate about (3, -1) by 2.5; (2, 0) → (5, -1) → (8, -1), which is 5 from (3, -1).

questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: the translation keeps the radius 2 and moves the center to (3, -1); the dilation by 5/2 about the center makes every radius 5, so the image is C₂; the check point lands on C₂.
